newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid corn/soy slide.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes mixed amid corn/soy slide.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mixed as a slide in corn and soybeans trimmed early gains, especially in the nearby months, traders said.
"It seems to be a trendless affair. It's broken out of a downtrend but seems to be trying to consolidate," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man Interntional.
Wheat held firm most of the session on support from the export sector.
USDA early Friday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 10 totalled 586,900 tonnes, above expectations for 250,000 to 450,000 tonnes.
Traders also said the CBOT markets, including wheat, were expected to remain volatile and were seeking direction amid conflicting weather forecasts.
"It may be Monday before we know where we're going from here, Monday will be a major swing day," a trader said.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed unchanged to six cents per bushel higher, with July unchanged at $3.25. September closed 1/4 cent higher at $3.31-3/4.

In spread dealings, FIMAT Futures did one-half million bushels of September/December at 14-3/4 cents premium December and USA Trading spread one half million March/December at nine to 9-1/2 cents, traders said.

Continental Grain sold two million bushels of September and bought one million September, traders said. FIMAT Futures bought two million bushels of September and USA Trading sold one million September, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, above the 16,810 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 400 September $3.80 calls at 1-1/2 cents, sold 400 March $4.00 calls at 12 cents and bought 500 September $3.50 calls at 4-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,700 contracts, below the 5,039 traded Wednesday.
